I — Arrival

Carved light,
low conversation.

A mezzanine off Fazal-e-Haq Road opens into warm stone, copper lamps and long shadows. The city stays outside.

II — Table

Set for the
slow hours.

Ivory linen, copper service, a candle that holds the whole table. Dinner here is measured in conversations, not courses.

III — Rooftop

The Margalla,
at dusk.

Upstairs the air changes. Hills on the horizon, string light overhead, the evening settling over Islamabad.

The Kitchen

Plates built for
sharing, late.

Soups that steam, wings with lacquer, tempura under a cold sauce, lemonades poured tall. A kitchen that cooks for a table of six as easily as for two.

01 — To Begin

Hot & Sour Soup

Dark, peppered broth with shiitake, ribboned egg and spring onion — the first bowl of every winter evening in Blue Area.

02 — Fire

Buffalo Wings

Glazed until the sauce catches the light, cooled by a herbed dip. Ordered by the table, finished without ceremony.

03 — From the Sea

Prawn Tempura

Six or nine pieces, fried light and loud, with a dark dipping sauce. Crisp holds all the way to the last one.

04 — The Long Table

Supreme Nachos

Cheese pulled across the tray, chilli and coriander through it. The dish that keeps a rooftop table talking past midnight.
